# Codex Mode for DeepSeek Harness

A Codex-style execution mode for DSH. It adds a switch at the top of the
permission menu, keeps a du

rable plan, emits visible progress while tools run,
and continues a turn that stops with unfinished

plan, emits visible progress while tools run,
and continues a turn that stops with unfinished work.

The important difference from a prompt-only mode: if the model emits a tool call
without text, the h

ost driver commits a short progress message **before** the
tool runs, as part of the durable assista

nt message. A long turn is not a silent
tool loop.
## What it does

- **Codex switch** at the top of the permission menu, above a divider. The
switch does not change th

e sandbox or approval level.
- **Remembered globally**: the last state is stored in the profile's
`c

odex_mode` storage domain. Turning it on or off applies to every live root
session; new and resumed

sessions inherit it automatically.
- **Visible progress** before every tool batch. The model's own c

ommentary is
kept; a missing one is inserted by the driver in the user's language.
- **Turn continua

tion** when the todo list still has unfinished work and the
assistant is not asking a question.
- **

Durable per-session identity** stored as `codex-read-only`,
`codex-workspace-write`, or `codex-dange

r-full-access`, so the mode appears in
the session log and survives resume.
- **Same safety gates**

for Full access and Auto review as the stock permission
control.
## Requirements

- DSH Desktop or Web with the Plugin Manager. Tested with DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`.
- The package declares `

engines.dsh: ^0.2.1-rc.1`; install it on a 0.2.1-rc.x
runtime.
- Git and network access to GitHub fo
r the first install.

h into **Plugins → Install

### After installing

1. Open any session.
2. Click the permission control at the bottom of the composer.
3. Turn on **Cod

ex Mode** at the top of the menu.
4. Pick `Read Only`, `Workspace Write`, or `Full access` exactly a

s before. The
mode and the permission level are independent.

HMR applies the change immediately in the desktop app. If your profile has HMR
disabled, restart DSH
after installation.

To remove it, open **Plugins → Codex Mode → Remove**, or ask the agent to remove
the bundle.
## Use
The menu has two dimensions:

- the Codex switch controls the execution protocol;
- the permission choices control the sandbox and

h controls the execution protocol;
- the permission choices control the sandbox and approval policy.

Turning Codex on while `Workspace Write` is selected moves every live root
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
The package is a DSH bundle with a Host half and a Web client half.

- `cordis.patch.yml` adds the three `codex-*` permission presets and mounts the
Host plugin.
- A pro

file-level `codex_mode` storage domain keeps `{ enabled, updatedAt }`.
The `/codex-mode on|off` comm

and writes it first, then applies the matching
`codex-*` or base preset to every live root session.

The `agent/created`
listener applies the remembered value to new and resumed root agents.
- The Host

plugin adds the `codex:mode` system-prompt section and wraps each
live agent's step. In Codex mode,

an `assistant/message` that contains only
tool calls gets a leading progress text block before it i

s committed; the
matching `text-chunks` record is added to the stream and tool-call block
indexes ar

e shifted so content and stream stay aligned.
- `agent/turn-stopping` provides one continuation stee

r when the plan is
unfinished and the reply is not a question.
- The Client plugin replaces the curr

ent-session permission control with the
same control plus the Codex row, keeping the original permis

sion glyphs and
the Full-access/Auto-review risk dialogs.

This is a Codex **step driver**, not a second tool runtime. DSH still owns turn
construction, tool d

ispatch, approvals, retries, compaction, and the event log.
A full fork of those systems would dupli

cate a large amount of tested
infrastructure; the driver changes the part users actually see: progre

ss output
and turn continuation.
### Why the progress line is provable

The line is not a UI status chip. In a test turn that explicitly told the model
not to emit text, th

e model's stream contained only reasoning and tool-call
chunks, with no `text-chunks`. The committed
assistant message was:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The matching stream indexes were reasoning `0`, text `1`, tool-call `2`. The
text could only come fr

om the Host driver. The test was run locally against DSH
`0.2.1-rc.3`; the session log itself is not

driver. The test was run locally against DSH
`0.2.1-rc.3`; the session log itself is not published.
## Scope and limitations

- The package targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.x`. It uses the live agent's `step` and the
session append bound

ary; a future DSH release can change those internals.
- It is not a complete Codex engine. Freeform

`apply_patch`, Codex-style
one-tool scheduling, shell/output limits, and Codex compaction thresholds

are
not implemented.
- The bundle overrides the `permission` row to add the `codex-*` presets. If y

ou
maintain custom permission presets in a profile, carry them into
cordis.patch.yml before installi

ng.
- The built-in `/permission` command also lists the `codex-*` identities. Use the
composer menu

or `/codex-mode on|off` for the global switch; a direct
`/permission` change is a per-session overri

de.
- The Settings default-permission selector lists the `codex-*` presets because
they are ordinary

permission presets; the composer menu is the intended place
to switch a running session.
